ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the closed rectangular conducting coil abcd rotates uniformly in a uniform magnetic field about the symmetry axis OO′ perpendicular to the magnetic induction lines. Observed along the OO′ direction, the coil rotates clockwise. It is known that the magnetic induction intensity of the uniform magnetic field is B, the number of turns of the coil is n, the side length of side ab is L1, the side length of side ad is L2, the resistance of the coil is R, and the angular velocity of rotation is ω. Then when the coil turns to the position shown in the figure, in what direction does the induced current in the coil flow?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the rectangular coil abcd is located in the plane of the paper; the left end of the top side is labeled b, and the right end is labeled a; the left end of the bottom side is labeled c, and the right end is labeled d; the uniform magnetic field B is represented by multiple horizontal arrows, directed to the right; the dashed line OO′ is the vertical rotation axis passing through the center of the coil; the figure also marks the angular velocity ω and states that, viewed along the OO′ direction, the coil rotates clockwise. Then reason: Take a→b→c→d→a as the positive circulation direction. According to the right-hand rule, when the four fingers bend along a→b→c→d→a, the direction pointed by the thumb is the area normal direction corresponding to this positive direction. According to the meaning of the problem, when observing the coil along the OO′ direction as it rotates clockwise, just after the coil passes the position shown in the figure, this positive area normal will deflect toward the side opposite to the magnetic field B. Therefore, the external magnetic flux calculated according to this positive normal is changing from zero to a negative value, that is, the change trend of the magnetic flux is increasing in the negative direction. By Lenz's law, the magnetic field produced by the induced current must hinder this change, so the induced current should produce a magnetic field along the positive normal direction. Then using the right-hand rule in reverse, the current direction is a→b→c→d→a.
